message.reasoning_content:
The user asks about PostgreSQL community support policy for major version 16, scheduled final release date, how long major versions are supported and when the clock begins, and whether installing a newer 16.x minor restarts the clock.

Facts I know: PostgreSQL community supports each major version for 5 years from its initial release. Version 16 was released September 14, 2023. So EOL would be November 2028 (typically the final release is in November of the 5th year). Actually PostgreSQL's versioning policy: each major release is supported for 5 years from date of initial release. E.g., PostgreSQL 11 released Oct 2018, EOL Nov 2023. Hmm, 5 years.

Let me verify with web sources: PostgreSQL versioning policy page (https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/) states "PostgreSQL major versions are supported for five years from their initial release." And version 16 released 2023-09-14; final release scheduled for 2028-11-09? Let me check the versioning page. Actually there's a table on that page listing version, supported, first release, final release... The "Versioning policy" page has a table listing each version with "Latest minor", "Supported", "First release", "EOL"? Let me search.

Also the question asks whether minor version upgrades restart the support clock — no, the clock begins at the initial major release (X.0), and minor releases don't extend it.

Let me do a websearch and webfetch. I should use both websearch and webfetch (required for success).

Search: "PostgreSQL versioning policy five years major versions supported".

Fetch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/

Also possibly the PostgreSQL 16 release announcement for the release date. Let's do that.

Note the cutoff: "public primary sources available by 2026-10-07". So the cutoff date is 2026-10-07. Question: is major version 16 supported at the cutoff? Yes, until Nov 2028.

Let's gather evidence.
